1. Fill in the blanks (i) Unlike poles of two magnets each other, whereas like poles each other. (ii) The materials that are attracted towards a magnet are called . (iii) The needle of a magnetic compass rests along the direction. (iv) A magnet always has poles.

2. State whether the following statements are True (T) or False (F). (i) A magnet can be broken into pieces to obtain a single pole. [ ] (ii) Similar poles of a magnet repel each other. [ ] (iii) Iron filings mostly stick in the middle of a bar magnet when it is brought near them. [ ] (iv) A freely suspended bar magnet always aligns with the north-south direction. [ ]   ­A magnet has two poles—the North pole and the South pole.   The poles of a magnet always exist in pairs. A single North pole or a single South pole cannot exist.   Magnetic materials are the materials that are attracted towards a magnet.   Non-magnetic materials are the materials that are not attracted towards a magnet.   A freely suspended magnet rests along the north-south direction.   The needle of a magnetic compass indicates the north-south direction.   When two magnets are brought close to each other, like poles (North-North, South-South) repel each other while unlike poles (North-South) attract each other.
